decided.singular: Four excursions rise well clear of the usual 5-25 band: about 51 at days 149-157, about 40 at 313-320, about 35 at 272-276, and about 36 at the start of the year (days 1-3). The next tallest hump, about 27 near day 106, does not separate as clearly.
decided.recurrence: The smooth curve shows evenly spaced humps, often about 13-14 days apart, with stronger ones repeating about every 27-28 days (for example 245, 273 and about 300, or 316 and 344). This is only moderately confident by eye and partly primed by the previous rendering.
decided.quarter: Q2 has the tallest peak (about 51 near day 152), a second burst near 163-166 (about 25) and a sustained run of 20-27 humps over days 92-125; Q4 has two big peaks but deeper lulls.

answer.guess: A smoothed daily geomagnetic activity index, likely daily ap or a running mean of ap derived from Kp.
